title: Text paragraph formatting: thread leading, margins, indent to SWF encoder
description:
The TextDisplayObject model carries letterSpacing (added in task 0789) but packages/swf/src/text.ts never reads it — the field is silently dropped on publish. Worse, the DefineEditText HasLayout block in encodeDefineEditText() hardcodes Leading=2, LeftMargin=0, RightMargin=0, Indent=0 regardless of what the author sets. The authoring canvas renderer (core/src/engine/renderer.ts) also ignores letterSpacing, so the stage preview does not match the published SWF.

Scope:

1. Model: add leading (SI16, line spacing extra in px), leftMargin, rightMargin, indent (UI16, px each) fields to TextDisplayObject in packages/core/src/engine/types.ts; update makeTextDisplayObject factory defaults (leading=0, margins=0).
2. SWF encoder: read obj.letterSpacing, obj.leading, obj.leftMargin, obj.rightMargin, obj.indent in encodeDefineEditText() instead of hardcoded values. Letter spacing in SWF is not a DefineEditText field — emit it by applying per-glyph advance adjustment in the glyph index array (or note it is a runtime-only TextFormat property and emit DoInitAction TextFormat.setTextFormat after place). Choose the simpler path: for now encode leading/margins/indent in HasLayout; document that letterSpacing requires runtime TextFormat and leave a TODO.
3. Authoring canvas: read obj.letterSpacing in renderer.ts renderText() and apply via ctx.letterSpacing (CSS text-spacing) or manual per-char advance loop so WYSIWYG matches runtime.
4. PropertiesPanel: add a Paragraph subsection (visible for all text types) with numeric fields for Leading (px), Left Margin (px), Right Margin (px), Indent (px). Wire to onUpdateObject.
5. Unit tests: extend packages/swf/src/__tests__/text.test.ts to verify non-zero Leading / LeftMargin / RightMargin / Indent values appear in the encoded HasLayout bytes.

Acceptance: (a) unit tests pass, (b) publishing a text field with leading=20 produces a SWF whose DefineEditText HasLayout Leading field equals 400 twips (20 * 20), (c) PropertiesPanel shows and updates the four paragraph fields.
